risks.note: Exposure to economic slowdowns, inflationary pressures and shifts in consumer sentiment that may adversely affect discretionary spending and overall demand. Mitigated through a multi-tier pricing architecture, continuous menu innovation and value engineering to offset input-cost inflation, and ongoing monitoring of macro indicators to recalibrate pricing and promotions. Management explicitly flags that near-term uncertainties relating to consumer demand and input costs will require close monitoring.
risks.risk: Macroeconomic & market risk - discretionary demand sensitivity

risks.note: Revenue volatility from festive cycles, regional demand patterns and evolving consumer preferences can hit store-level performance and capacity utilisation. Addressed with advanced analytics and predictive demand modelling, agile workforce and inventory planning, and targeted campaigns and product bundling to drive traffic in lean periods.

Process inefficiencies, execution gaps or dependency on key personnel may disrupt operations or impact service quality across a 2,000-plus store network. Mitigated by clearly defined standardised operating procedures across locations, a strengthened governance structure with defined roles, accountability and escalation mechanisms, and leadership pipeline development with structured succession planning.
risks.risk: Operational & organizational risk - execution and key-person dependency

risks.note: Supplier concentration, logistics constraints, geopolitical factors and commodity price volatility can affect availability and cost structures for a food business. Managed through a diversified, geographically distributed supplier network, long-term strategic sourcing agreements for cost predictability, technology-enabled supply-chain visibility with real-time inventory tracking, and periodic supplier audits and risk assessments.

Attracting, retaining and upskilling talent in a high-attrition industry can impact service delivery and growth plans; the BRSR shows permanent-employee turnover remaining elevated. Mitigated by structured recruitment, onboarding and performance management, continuous investment in training and leadership development, engagement and wellness programmes with performance-linked incentives, and a focus on diversity, equity and inclusion.
risks.risk: Human capital risk in a high-attrition industry

risks.note: As the business becomes increasingly technology-enabled - with digital ordering, kiosks, analytics and data-driven HR and supply-chain systems - risks relate to system downtime and scalability limitations, making resilience of digital platforms central to operations.

Identified in the BRSR double-materiality assessment as a material risk with negative financial implications: any compromise in food safety and quality may result in customer dissatisfaction along with regulatory scrutiny, notices and penalties. Mitigated through rigorous hygiene standards from preparation to storage under strict SOPs, regular evaluation of stores by franchisors, third-party agencies and regulators, and sourcing of all critical raw materials from GFSI-compliant suppliers.

BRSR-identified material risk with negative financial implications: inadequate waste management can result in regulatory non-compliance, and improper disposal may lead to environmental contamination of soil, water and air. Governed by the Company's Environment and Waste Management Policy covering waste reduction, segregation, timely disposal, hygiene standards and regulatory compliance.
